findings.claim: No state air permit, draft permit, public notice, or construction-stormwater coverage for any of the nine plants is indexed by web search. MDEQ, ADEM, SC DES, Shelby County Health Dept, GA EPD and TDEC were all checked; schedules remain company guidance.
findings.detail: Targeted domain searches of mdeq.ms.gov, adem.alabama.gov, des.sc.gov and shelbytnhealth.com returned only generic program pages or unrelated facilities. The permit databases (MDEQ enSearch, ADEM eFile, SC DES ePermitting, GA EPD GEOS, TDEC Dataviewer) are query applications that the search engine does not crawl. Absence of evidence is not evidence of no permit.

findings.claim: Hitachi Gallman MS: $528M plant for 10-160 MVA units up to 230 kV. Construction is to begin late 2026 and production in 2029. No groundbreaking had been reported as of Oct 11, 2026.
findings.detail: Announced Sep 15, 2026. The press release describes construction start as future (late 2026). No MDEQ notice was found.

findings.claim: Gallman is partly a relocation. It sits ~6.5 miles from Crystal Springs and is more than twice its size, and Crystal Springs production is to move to Gallman when it is complete. Net new US capacity is therefore roughly one Crystal Springs, not the full Gallman output.
findings.detail: This matches Utility Dive's 'double US production' framing: if a site 2x Crystal Springs replaces Crystal Springs, the net add is about 1x. Computed reasoning, not a company statement of net units. Whether the Crystal Springs building is closed, sold or repurposed is unknown.
findings.entity: Hitachi Energy, Crystal Springs and Gallman MS

findings.claim: Gallman job counts conflict: the company says more than 700 jobs, while Big Energy News says more than 1,600.

HD Hyundai Electric broke ground on Montgomery plant #2 on Mar 6, 2026. The plant is ~312,000 sq ft inside the existing site, costs $200M, and adds 50% to EHV output with 765 kV build and test capability.
findings.detail: 200 new jobs. Total HD-HPT investment in Montgomery reaches $277M. This is the only plant in the set with both a dated groundbreaking and an EHV scope.
findings.entity: HD Hyundai Electric (Hyundai Power Transformers USA), Montgomery AL

findings.claim: HD Hyundai's completion date conflicts: the company says April 2027, while the Montgomery Chamber says the plant opens mid-2027.

The only Hyundai-named ADEM notice found is a synthetic-minor (SMOP) air permit notice dated Oct 1, 2026 for Hyundai Transys Georgia Seating System, LLC in Montgomery County. That is a seating maker, not the transformer plant.
findings.detail: It should not be cited as evidence for the HD Hyundai Electric transformer plant. No ADEM notice for Hyundai Power Transformers was found.

findings.claim: VTC Muscle Shoals: a 600,000 sq ft plant on ~90 acres at the Shoals Research Airpark (Colbert County) with a planned Norfolk Southern rail spur, 2-500 MVA, 1,100 jobs. Construction was to start 'immediately' after May 19, 2026, with production in Jan 2028.
findings.detail: No groundbreaking ceremony, site-work or hiring news after May 2026 was found. One outlet's mention of ground already broken is a single unconfirmed report. The only Muscle Shoals ADEM notice (Apr 21, 2026) is the City's Class V UIC permit for stormwater basins and is unrelated.
findings.entity: Virginia Transformer Corp, Muscle Shoals AL

findings.claim: VTC's Rincon GA expansion has slipped and been scaled back. The Nov 2025 announcement promised ~70% more production about one year after a Jan 2026 start. A later VTC groundbreaking release cites a 50% increase in installed capacity and completion in March 2027.
findings.detail: Gov. Kemp (Nov 20, 2025): $40M and 400+ jobs at 2789 GA-21, Effingham County. The May 19, 2026 Muscle Shoals release also gives a March 2027 completion for Rincon. This contradicts the baseline's 'Rincon +70% (2026)'.
findings.entity: Virginia Transformer (Georgia Transformer Corp), Rincon GA

findings.claim: The Rincon scope includes new Vapor Phase Drying equipment, plus vertical winding machines, core-building machinery and a transformer prep area. VPD typically uses a solvent, so it is the item most likely to need a GA EPD air permit or modification. No such permit was found.
findings.detail: The equipment list comes from VTC's release. That VPD triggers a permit is an inference, not a finding. The only Rincon permit PDFs surfaced (EPA-hosted 2621-103-0007-V-06-0) belong to the Georgia-Pacific paper mill.

findings.claim: Eaton Jonesville is a conversion of the former Belk distribution center at 6802 Furman L. Fendley Hwy, not a greenfield build. Union County received a $10M Rural Infrastructure Fund grant for the retrofit. Production and hiring are slated for 2027, with 700 jobs.
findings.detail: Investment is $340M. A late-2026 Eaton release reportedly repeats the 2027 start without a progress update. No SC DES air construction permit was found.

findings.claim: Hyosung HICO Memphis is two stacked expansions. The first (May 14, 2025) is $51M and 123 jobs at the 360,000 sq ft plant on ~200 acres. The second (Nov 12, 2025) is $157M and 240 jobs for a new facility adding 50% capacity. A Hyosung release targets more than 50% added capacity by 2028.
Hyosung's design-build contractor, Alston Construction, posted a groundbreaking for the Shelby County expansion on Nov 24, 2025.
findings.detail: The excerpt had no schedule detail. No Shelby County Health Dept air notice for Hyosung was found.

findings.claim: Howard's $100M Ellisville expansion ($55M building, $45M equipment) raises the plant's maximum ratings from 168 MVA, 230 kV primary and 900 kV BIL to 250 MVA (ONAN), 345 kV and 1175 kV BIL.
findings.detail: The company release says 100 jobs. WDAM's groundbreaking report says ~150.
findings.entity: Howard Industries (Howard Power Solutions), Ellisville MS

findings.claim: Howard held a groundbreaking at Ellisville on Apr 2, 2026. One outlet says the building expansion completes by Sep 2026 and the full project by end-2026.
Separately, MDA announced in June 2025 a $236.95M Howard project across Clarke, Jones and Simpson counties, creating 450 jobs and to be completed within five years.
Hitachi Alamo TN broke ground on Aug 20, 2025. The expansion adds more than 60,000 sq ft (35k manufacturing, 20k warehouse, 5k office) for dry HVDC and AC bushings up to 800 kV, with ~100 jobs.
findings.detail: Investment figures differ: the company says $106M, TNECD says an initial $97M. Trade press calls it a two-year project, implying ~2027 (inference). No TDEC record was found.

findings.claim: Central Moloney's Bay County FL site is operating. It makes single-phase pole-mount transformers in a leased 140,000 sq ft building at Venture Crossings Enterprise Center, owned by The St. Joe Company. Capex is ≥$25M (initially >$20M) for ≥200 jobs.
findings.detail: Announced Jan 2022. Florida's Great Northwest says the Bay site is one of two Northwest Florida locations, together employing 550 people with $75M of capex at full capacity. The second site was not identified. This resolves the baseline's 'start date unverified', though no exact first-production date was found. Computed: $25M / 200 jobs = $125k capex per job.
findings.entity: Central Moloney Inc., Panama City Beach (Bay County) FL

findings.claim: Central Moloney is actively hiring in Panama City and Panama City Beach. Posted pay is $23-27/hr for Transformer Repair Technicians and $52K-56K for a Production Team Lead.

Computed capex per announced job varies about 8x. Central Moloney's leased building is ~$125k per job ($25M/200). Eaton's brownfield conversion is ~$486k ($340M/700). Hitachi Gallman's greenfield is ≤$754k ($528M/700). Howard's medium-power expansion is $0.67-1.0M ($100M/150-100).
findings.detail: Inputs come from the cited company and state releases. These are computed values, and the job counts are announcement targets.

result.analysis:
Permits do not yet confirm any plant's schedule. No state air permit, construction-stormwater NOI or throughput/VOC limit was found for any of the nine plants (se-permits-none-indexed). The permit databases are not crawlable, so the next step is direct database queries or records requests.

Non-permit evidence still separates the plants:
- **Physically underway:** HD Hyundai Montgomery #2 (groundbreaking Mar 6, 2026; se-hdh-groundbreak), Hyosung Memphis (Nov 24, 2025; se-hyosung-groundbreak), Hitachi Alamo bushings (Aug 2025; se-alamo), Howard Ellisville (Apr 2026, due end-2026; se-howard-timing) and VTC Rincon.
- **Least verified:** the two largest job counts. Hitachi Gallman has not started; construction begins late 2026 for 2029 output (se-gallman-scope). VTC Muscle Shoals has no confirmed groundbreaking or site work since its May 2026 announcement, yet guides to January 2028 output (se-vtc-ms-scope).

Four points bear on a would-be builder:
1. **The incumbent wave is smaller and later than the headlines.**
   - Gallman partly replaces Crystal Springs, so the net addition is about one Crystal Springs, not a full new plant (se-gallman-replaces-crystal-springs).
   - VTC Rincon slipped from ~+70% by end-2026 to +50% by March 2027 (se-vtc-rincon-slip).
   - HD Hyundai's date already reads April or mid-2027 depending on the source (se-hdh-date-conflict).
   - Treat every 2027-29 date as likely to slip 3-6 months. That slightly widens the window for an entrant shipping in 2028.
2. **Howard is moving up-market fast.** Ellisville goes from 168 MVA/230 kV to 250 MVA/345 kV by end-2026 (se-howard-ratings), and a separate $237M, 450-job program runs through ~2030 (se-howard-2025-mda). That is direct competition in the 10-100 MVA band an entrant would grow into, and it makes Howard harder to buy cheaply.
3. **Re-using existing buildings is the proven low-capex route.**
   - Eaton is converting a former Belk distribution center with a $10M state retrofit grant (se-eaton-brownfield).
   - Central Moloney is already producing single-phase pole-mounts in a leased 140k sq ft spec building for about $25M (se-cmi-operating).
   - Computed capex per announced job: ~$125k for Central Moloney versus ~$486k for Eaton and up to ~$754k for Gallman (se-capex-per-job-computed). This supports the buy-or-convert entry over a $340-530M greenfield.
4. **Air permitting looks manageable but unverified.** VTC's Rincon scope includes vapor-phase drying (se-vtc-rincon-vpd). An entrant should budget a minor-source or synthetic-minor air permit for VPD solvent and varnish/paint VOC, and should pull a comparable permit from GA EPD or MDEQ to size the limits before choosing a site.

findings.claim: Hitachi Energy broke ground on its $457M South Boston large power transformer expansion on June 29, 2026, with 825 new jobs.
findings.detail: WFXR reports 826 jobs (https://www.wfxrtv.com/news/local-news/southside-virginia-news/hitachi-energy-invests-457-million-in-south-boston-transformer-plant/). FieldNews, citing ENR, says the new building is >300,000 sq ft with >120 ft assembly bays, a 375-ton crane and a four-story office (W). WFXR also reports 136 workforce apartments/townhomes being built in Halifax County.

findings.claim: One post-groundbreaking summary puts South Boston production at about 2029, later than the baseline's ~2028.
findings.detail: The search tool attributed the phrase 'expected to reach production around 2029' to one of the result pages, either fieldnews.net or mgrid.org (https://mgrid.org/2026/06/29/hitachi-energy-breaks-ground-on-457m-virginia-transformer-factory-largest-in-us-amid-data-center-grid-crunch/). Hitachi's own release should be checked for the start date. A Jun 2026 groundbreaking for a >300k sq ft LPT hall makes 2029 more plausible than 2028 (judgment).

findings.claim: A targeted search of Virginia DEQ, Town Hall and Halifax County/South Boston domains found no air-permit registration, public notice or building permit for the Hitachi South Boston expansion.
findings.detail: This is negative evidence from a search, not proof that no permit exists. The myDEQ portal (https://portal.deq.virginia.gov/) is not search-indexed.

findings.claim: A 2026 Siemens Energy job posting says the Charlotte transformer facility is planned to be built by late 2026 for production to begin, against an original early-2026 production target.
findings.detail: The search tool did not say whether the language came from posting 298177 (Process Engineer, Transformer Factory Greenfield Build) or 301578 (Manufacturing Supervisor, LPT). The original 2024 plan was production in early 2026, 24 LPT/yr rising to 57 (https://www.siemens-energy.com/us/en/home/press-releases/siemens_energy_addresses_shortage_US_powertransformers_invests_new_factory.html).

findings.claim: The original Charlotte transformer project was a $149,859,000 investment with 475 jobs, supported by a state JDIG approved by NC's Economic Investment Committee, with city and county participation.
findings.detail: Also https://news.mecknc.gov/siemens-energy-selects-mecklenburg-county-upcoming-expansion. Siemens' own stories cite up to 559 direct operating jobs and 285 construction jobs, and a later '$400M expansion, >600 jobs'. These are different counts and should not be added. No JDIG ID or MCAQ permit was found.

findings.claim: In Feb 2026 Siemens Energy announced $421M of further NC investment and ~500 jobs, focused on generators and resuming gas-turbine manufacturing in Charlotte rather than transformers.
findings.detail: A City of Charlotte item (Feb 2026) separately says Siemens will make additional investments to expand LPT manufacturing and service capacity, but gives no LPT-specific figure (https://www.charlottenc.gov/City-News/Siemens-Energy-Expands-Operations-in-Charlotte-Creating-More-Jobs).

findings.claim: Prolec GE's Goldsboro second plant ($140M, 330 jobs, 220 to 420 medium power transformers/yr) broke ground on Mar 17, 2026, and the company expects to complete the investment by Dec 31, 2027.
findings.detail: Dec 31, 2027 and the unit figures are from https://businessnc.com/prolec-ge-plans-140-million-investment-to-create-330-jobs-in-wayne-county-expansion/. The state incentive announcement is https://www.commerce.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2025/05/14/governor-stein-announces-additional-330-new-jobs-coming-wayne-county-production-facility. The Goldsboro Daily News dated the event Mar 18. Computed: +200 units/yr, +91% (420/220 = 1.91).

findings.claim: Searches of NC DAQ's permitted-facility lists (dated 9/30/2026 and 7/8/2026) did not surface Prolec GE in Wayne County or Pennsylvania Transformer in Hoke County. The only Raeford facility returned was Burlington Industries (permit 4700001).
findings.value: Burlington Industries Raeford 4700001; Wayne County permits in 9600xxx range
findings.detail: The PDF text was garbled in extraction, so absence is not proven. Transformer assembly (varnish/VPI, paint) may fall under small-source exemptions or general permits. A DAQ facility search by name would confirm.

findings.claim: Rather than build, ERMCO bought a finished speculative shell, Building A of Virgin Industrial Park at 15784 W. Hatcher Rd, Waddell. It paid $91M to Invesco Real Estate, per Maricopa County public records.
findings.detail: The building was developed by IndiCap and Invesco with an $88M construction loan; Cushman & Wakefield brokered. Computed: $91,000,000 / 566,121 sq ft = ~$161/sq ft for a new West Valley shell. ERMCO's own release (Jan 21, 2026) gives the address, 566,000 sq ft and 4,070 sq ft of office (https://www.ermco-eci.com/ermco-to-open-new-manufacturing-facility-in-maricopa-county/). The deed date and recording number were not captured.

findings.claim: ERMCO's Arizona 3-phase plant targets operation in 2027 with >500 jobs, but Arizona Commerce Authority wording describes a first plant operational in 2026 and a second in 2027.
findings.detail: Most trade coverage says 2027 (e.g., https://www.powermag.com/ermco-expands-transformer-manufacturing-west-with-new-arizona-facility/). The ACA two-plant language is unexplained. No Maricopa County Air Quality Department permit was found.

findings.claim: Adjacent spec buildings at the same industrial park were still marketed for lease: Building B with 213,765 sf available and Building C with a 79,604 sf minimum.
findings.detail: Listing data and possibly stale. It shows ready shells next to ERMCO's plant in the West Valley labor shed.

findings.claim: Giga Energy's ~60,000 sq ft Houston medium-voltage plant was slated to start production in Q1 2026, with 25 initial jobs growing to ~100. Trade press later headlined that the factory had opened, but stated capacity conflicts: 1,000+ units/yr on the company site versus >3,000 in some outlets.
findings.detail: The announcement is at https://www.bicmagazine.com/departments/engineering-construction/giga-energy-announces-new-houston-manufacturing-facility/ and the opening headline at https://transformer-magazine.com/news/giga-energy-opens-houston-transformer-factory/ (opening date not captured). No street address, TCEQ registration or local abatement was found.

findings.claim: VanTran expanded into a ~430,000 sq ft former Sherwin-Williams distribution center (~700 jobs over five years). Incentives were a property-tax phase-in and a Waco-McLennan County EDC grant, plus a Texas Enterprise Zone nomination for up to $960,000 in state sales-tax refunds, which Waco City Council approved.
findings.value: 430,000 sq ft; up to $960,000 Enterprise Zone refund
findings.detail: Capex figures conflict: >$20M (release), $33M (local report) and 'nearly $100M' retrofitting the former Sherwin-Williams DC (https://wacotrib.com/news/local/business/article_cb939de8-0380-4d0c-bc2b-6c8d0fd3c937.html). The $960k figure is from a mirror of a Waco Tribune report (https://www.rgruiying.com/news/vantran-expanding-waco-transformermaking-operation.html, W). No Chapter 380 agreement or TCEQ record was found. It shows the fast brownfield-warehouse conversion path.

findings.claim: PTT's Raeford expansion includes a new 150,000 sq ft pad-mounted distribution transformer plant. Construction completion is expected in Q4 2026 and first shipments in early 2027.
findings.value: 150,000 sq ft; complete Q4 2026; shipments early 2027
findings.detail: The state describes >$102.5M, 217 jobs and 300,000 sq ft across two Raeford facilities, with groundbreaking on Dec 10, 2025 (https://www.commerce.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2025/12/10/governor-stein-celebrates-pennsylvania-transformer-technology-groundbreaking-hoke-county). The baseline listed PTT only as a 5-750 MVA power maker; this adds a Quanta-backed entrant in the pad-mount segment a newcomer would target.

findings.claim: NCCR Invests, the North Carolina Railroad's economic-development arm, granted $400,000 for rail service to PTT's Raeford expansion.
findings.detail: No One NC grant was found in the results.

findings.claim: The Erie County IDA held a public hearing on Aug 25, 2026, and its September 2026 board agenda lists an inducement resolution of $2,194,264 in incentives against a $71,203,457 investment. The incentives are sales/use tax exemption and real property tax abatement (PILOT).
findings.detail: Hearing notice: https://www.ecidany.com/event/101464/public-hearing-niagara-power-transformer. WBEN reports $1.7M sales-tax breaks plus a multi-year PILOT, with a board vote set for Sep 23, 2026. The final vote was not confirmed. Computed: incentives are 3.1% of investment (2,194,264 / 71,203,457).

findings.claim: NYPA approved $4.5M for the >$71M 'Niagara Power 50 Initiative'. The project is a new 96,000 sq ft plant on Dale Road plus a later 32,000 sq ft addition to the 121,000 sq ft plant, with the workforce rising from 146 to 219.
findings.value: $4.5M NYPA; +96k and +32k sq ft; 146 to 219 workers
findings.detail: Scope and jobs are from WBEN (https://www.audacy.com/wben/news/local/niagara-power-transformer-eyes-71m-expansion). The production gain is reported as +45% (WBEN) or +50% (state-linked). Computed: total public support is ~$6.69M (2,194,264 + 4,500,000), or 9.4% of $71,203,457. Construction start was not evidenced; the project was still in IDA approval in Sep 2026, against the baseline's 90 to 140 units/yr framing.

findings.claim: JST's Wytheville plant, its eleventh factory worldwide, is about 45,000 sq ft across two buildings in Fairview Industrial Park. Planned output is ~150 units in 2026 rising to 1,000 from 2027, with 25-30 manufacturing and 10-20 office hires.
findings.detail: Dates conflict: one JST release is dated Mar 13, 2025 while later coverage dates the opening to May 2026. No VEDP or Wythe County incentive or permit record was found. The small footprint and headcount suggest final assembly or kitting of imported active parts rather than full core-and-coil manufacture (judgment).

findings.claim: Several sources point to Hainan Jinpan Smart Technology (China) as JST's parent. JST says it began in 1993 in Haikou, China; Crunchbase lists 'Hainan Jinpan Intelligent Technology' as an alternate name; and US import records show Hainan Jinpan Smart Technology and Jinpan Electric Group as shippers.
findings.value: Origin Haikou 1993; pad-mounts made in Yangzhou (Jiangsu); factories in Wuhan (2021) and Malaysia (2025)
findings.detail: Supporting sources: https://manufacturing-today.com/news/after-china-mexico-and-malaysia-jst-power-equipment-continues-its-expansion-with-a-new-us-factory-in-virginia/ and https://www.importgenius.com/importers/jst-power-equipment-inc. No source states the ownership chain outright; confirm with the Virginia SCC entity record and Jinpan's annual report subsidiary list. If EO 14420 applies an ownership/control test, JST's 1,000 units/yr and its Yangzhou-built pad-mount imports are exposed.

findings.claim: On Aug 13, 2026 Heron Power chose Morgan Hill, CA for its first large-scale factory: a conversion of a former 286,000 sq ft distribution warehouse. Terms are >$100M investment, >600 jobs, a $26.4M CalCompetes award and capacity of up to 10,000 Heron Links/yr (>40 GW), with commercial production in late 2027.
findings.detail: Also reported by DCD (https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/crusoe-backed-transformer-manufacturer-heron-power-selects-morgan-hill-california-as-site-of-first-large-scale-factory/). Site preparation was to begin immediately. Lease or purchase is unknown. On Sep 21, 2026 Heron signed an RWE pilot with a path to a multi-year capacity reservation (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/21/3365509/0/en/heron-power-and-rwe-sign-pilot-agreement-outline-path-to-multi-year-capacity-reservation.html). Computed: CalCompetes is at most 26% of the stated >$100M investment.

result.analysis:
No plant schedule in this domain could be verified against an agency permit, certificate of occupancy or stormwater record. Agency portals (VA DEQ myDEQ, MCAQ, MCAQD, TCEQ) are not search-indexed, and NC DAQ's statewide list did not surface Prolec or PTT [hitachi-sb-no-permit, ncdaq-list-negative]. Every date below is still company guidance, cross-checked against incentive records and press.

Three points matter for a would-be builder.

1. **The segment a newcomer would target is filling up faster than the baseline showed, including outside the Southeast.**
   - PTT, owned by Quanta, is adding a 150k sq ft pad-mount plant in Raeford that ships in early 2027 [ptt-raeford-padmount].
   - ERMCO skipped construction and bought a finished 566k sq ft West Valley shell for $91M (~$161/sq ft computed) for 2027 3-phase output [ermco-az-91m]. That weakens the "site outside the Southeast" edge in the Southwest specifically.
   - Giga (1,000+ units) and JST (1,000/yr from 2027) add more medium-voltage and pad-mount volume [giga-houston-status, jst-wytheville-site].

2. **Buying or converting an existing building is now the dominant fast route.** ERMCO (spec shell), VanTran (former Sherwin-Williams DC) and Heron (286k sq ft warehouse) all took it [vantran-waco-incentives, heron-morgan-hill]. Unleased spec space remains next to ERMCO [waddell-spec-shells]. For distribution-class work, which needs no 375-ton cranes or 120 ft bays, an entrant can copy this path and ship in roughly 12-18 months. This supports the round-1 advice to buy or expand rather than build greenfield.

3. **Large-power capacity keeps slipping, but that gap is not one a newcomer can reach.**
   - Siemens Charlotte production moves to 2027 [siemens-clt-latepost].
   - Hitachi South Boston only broke ground in June 2026, so 2029 looks more likely than 2028 [hitachi-sb-groundbreak, hitachi-sb-2029].
   - Niagara was still in IDA approval in September 2026 [niagara-ecida, niagara-nypa-scope].
   - Only Prolec Goldsboro has an investment deadline (Dec 31, 2027) consistent with its stated date [prolec-gso-deadline].

**JST's likely Jinpan ownership is the most decision-relevant new lead** [jst-jinpan-link, W]. If EO 14420 adopts an ownership/control test, up to 1,000 units/yr of pad-mount supply in Virginia, plus JST's Yangzhou-built imports, could be cut off. That would open room for a domestic pad-mount entrant.

**Incentive benchmarks:**
- Niagara: ~9.4% of capex from ECIDA plus NYPA (computed).
- Heron: CalCompetes $26.4M on >$100M.
- VanTran: Enterprise Zone up to $960k.
- PTT: $400k rail grant.

Local packages are modest. Plan on 3-10% of capex, not a decisive subsidy.
